content.recommendation_summary: Early angiography with subsequent PCI if required is the recommended standard of care after successful fibrinolysis for STEMI patients; transfer to a PCI-capable centre for angiography within ~2–24 h is supported.
content.timing_of_PCI_after_fibrinolysis: Optimal delay not clearly defined; trials show wide variation (median 1.3 to 17 h). Based on available data a time window for PCI of approximately 2–24 h after successful lysis is recommended.
content.benefit_and_safety: Routine early PCI after fibrinolysis demonstrated benefit without increased risk of major adverse events (stroke or major bleeding) across investigated patient subgroups.
content.comparison_of_fibrinolytic_agents: Some information on comparisons of fibrinolytic agents is provided in the Supplementary data online, Section 6.3.1.
content.hazards_and_contraindications: Information regarding hazards of, and contraindications to, fibrinolysis is provided in the Supplementary data online, Section 6.3.2.
content.patients_not_undergoing_reperfusion_over: Management of ACS patients not undergoing reperfusion is discussed in the Supplementary data online, Section 5.2.
content.patients_not_candidates_for_invasive_cor: Information regarding the management of NSTE-ACS patients who are not candidates for invasive angiography is provided in the Supplementary data online, Section 5.2.1.
content.patients_with_CAD_not_amenable_to_revasc: Management information for ACS patients with coronary artery disease not amenable to revascularization is provided in the Supplementary data online, Section 5.2.2.
